text:
Alex R: quick heads-up — the SLO card in console is useful but we're getting a lot of noisy p99/5m alerts from small tenants. thinking we should surface a sampling + soft-quiet-window policy in the UI so product teams can opt in/out without patching alerting rules
Maya: +1. we currently have global sampling but no per-tenant knobs. UI surface should include sample_rate, quiet_window, and a preview of estimated alerts/hour
Kevin: agree. also add a 'notify_budget' field so routing can prefer high-tier channels until budget exhausted. we can expose 'notify_budget' as a slider (0-100) in the console
Alex R: sketch of an example rule we could generate from the UI (pseudo):
```json
{
  "slo_id": "svc.request_latency",
  "window": "5m",
  "threshold": "p99>800ms",
  "sample_rate": 0.2,
  "quiet_window_secs": 1800,
  "notify_budget": 75,
  "routing": { "primary": "pager", "fallback": "email" },
  "telemetry_tags": ["tenant_id", "alert_fingerprint"]
}
```
Maya: love the telemetry_tags — add `exposure_bucket` too so we can compute alerts_per_hour_per_bucket for safe rollouts
Jess: edgecase — bursts shorter than quiet_window might still be important (deploy-time regressions). we should allow an override flag `bypass_quiet_for_deployment=true` tied to rollout metadata
sre-bot: policy-sim run for sample_rate=0.2 and quiet_window=1800: estimated alerts/hr reduction = 48%, false positive delta = -3% (sim on last 2w of data) :bar_chart:
Kevin: nice. implementation notes: API shape should accept both explicit rule JSON (above) and a compact form from console. keep ids stable so rollouts can patch sample_rate without replacing rule id
Alex R: UX question — should we expose absolute threshold edits (eg p99 -> 900ms) or only relative sensitivity (lenient/strict/critical) to keep consistency across tenants?
Maya: prefer relative presets by default (lenient/normal/strict) with an advanced toggle to set explicit thresholds. reduces support load
Jess: rollout plan: 1) add UI toggle + preview + dry-run API 2) beta for internal tenants 3) canary to 10% of tenants by exposure_bucket 4) monitor `alerts_per_hour_per_tenant`, `alert_ack_latency`, `false_positive_rate`
Kevin: telemetry: add `alert_fingerprint` in emitted event, and include `sample_rate` used when firing so we can offline-correct metrics. Also emit `policy_sim_id` when preview used
Alex R: action items:
- @Maya to mock console flow and payloads (due EOD Fri)
- @Kevin to spec API contract for sample_rate/notify_budget and stable ids (PR next week)
- @Jess to add deployment-bypass flag design and testcases (start Mon)
- @sre-bot to run policy-sim on random 5k tenants and post results here (once Kevin has contract)
Maya: acked. I'll include the preview estimation UI (alerts/hr, P99 impact, cost delta)
Jess: one more nit — we should persist the last_preview_snapshot so ops can repro a tenant's pre-change state if they escalate
Alex R: agreed. let's keep the console default conservative (lenient) and make advanced controls opt-in. thanks all :thumbsup:
Kevin: FYI i'll add a short compatibility shim so older alerting rules map to the new compact representation during rollout
Maya: will post mock screenshots in this thread when ready
Alex R: moving to RFC once mocks land. keeping thread open for any other edgecases
Jess: flagged a potential regulatory case where quiet_window might hide PII exfil alerts — will file a checklist item in RFC
Kevin: cool, adding that to API privacy review
Alex R: thanks — ping me if you need data slices for the policy-sim
